items.description: "The new JenkinsPipelineUtils method: (deploy repo, values path, {YAML path -> tag}) -> clone, update, commit, push" exists in the shared library, and its values-path parameter carries the whole set of files one call must move rather than the single path D45 named: D45's signature predates D47, which requires both stage files to be written in one commit, so a call that can only name chart/values.yaml cannot satisfy it (argo-cd/decisions.md:466-471 for D45's mechanism, :495-496 for the one-commit constraint).
evidence: AnsibleSpecs/argo-cd/decisions.md:495-496 (D47: both stage files in one commit)
JenkinsPipelineUtils/vars/ — 7 files, no clone/commit/push precedent to model on

items.description: The method's write is surgical: comments, key order and every key it was not given survive; a YAML path the values file does not already hold is an error rather than a silently created key; and a run whose tags are unchanged commits and pushes nothing, saying so.

The GitHub credential the push uses reaches neither the build log nor the deploy repo's history, following the estate's existing clone-edit-push precedent (/work/HomelabTerraformProvider/Jenkinsfile:82-95).

The library still loads for every job in the estate: the operator re-runs one trivial library-loading Jenkins job that changes nothing and the output is handed back. vars/* compile together on load, so a syntax error is estate-wide (JenkinsPipelineUtils/vars/, 7 files, no tests or CI).
evidence: JenkinsPipelineUtils/vars/*.groovy — compiled together on library load
19 Jenkinsfiles across /work load the library unpinned (`library identifier: 'JenkinsPipelineUtils'`)
/work/Ansible/Jenkinsfile.architecture:1-20 — candidate canary: loads the library, validates a YAML, archives it

items.description: "Move the seven image pins out of KubeCoderDeploy/chart/values.yaml into config/{dev,prd}/values.yaml — dev <n>, prd prd-<n> (D47). They sit at dev-511 today." — both stage files name all seven on the same build number and chart/values.yaml names no tag for any of them. The number is the newest dev-<n> the registry actually held when the phase ran, not 511: dev-511 has been evicted and can never be reproduced, so Ruling 4 has the phase choose at run time and both written tags are forward references slice 012's cutover creates.
evidence: http://registry:5000/v2/kubecoder-<name>/tags/list, re-queried 2026-09-20: dev-428..dev-509 then dev-514..dev-523 for all seven; no dev-511, no 511, no prd-511
/work/DockerImages/registry-cleanup/app/main.py:283-299 (the newest-10 per-prefix cap that evicted it)

items.description: "The committed default tag is a real <n>, never latest (D37)" — strengthened by D47 to no default at all and by Ruling 6 to a chart that refuses to render: with a stage values file missing any one of the seven, helm template fails with a message naming the key. Removing the default alone does not do that — an absent concatenated suffix renders an untagged reference and helm exits 0, and an absent controllerConfig.images key drops silently out of the controller's ConfigMap — so the guard is in the chart, where it protects a hand-edited stage file at sync time, with the gate checking the same property from outside.
evidence: AnsibleSpecs/argo-cd/decisions.md:396-398 (the D37 amendment: never a default at all — and its 'fails to render' claim, which Ruling 6 records as untrue of a concatenated tag)

items.description: "Invert KubeCoderDeploy/tests/render-chart.py's check_stage_values, which fails the gate on any image key in a stage file — the exact opposite of D47" — kc project test is green, and the gate now fails on D47's inverse: an image tag back in chart/values.yaml, a stage file missing one of the seven, a prd tag without its prd- prefix, or the two stage files naming different builds.
evidence: KubeCoderDeploy/tests/render-chart.py:71,158-167,188-208,311-353 (PIN regex and the three readers of chart/values.yaml)
KubeCoderDeploy `kc project test` green at plan time: build-deps, render-chart, terraform all OK

items.description: No coverage is lost in the gate rework: every image and pull-policy property the render gate asserts today either still holds or has a named successor, and images.tunnelReclaim keeps its floating reference and its check.

"Repoint everything keyed on the tag prefix" resolves to nothing to repoint (D47): this slice changes no file in registry-cleanup, collect-versions or the version-poller, and the evidence that none of them needs a change still holds.

items.description: Nothing live moves: no stage is deployed, redeployed or repointed by this slice, and KubeCoder keeps running from HelmCharts until slice 012's cutover. The method has no caller and the relocated pins no reader — Ruling 1's accepted consequence, and the reason this slice's verification is static.

Slice 012's slice.md carries the work Ruling 1 sent it: R2 — Build-Main's rewrite — stated as B.3 states it, beside the R4 entry already there, with this slice's grounding behind it (G5, G6, G8, G10, G12); and its 'Depends on' line names what slice 011 actually delivers instead of "011 (CI commits pins)", which Ruling 1 made false.
evidence: AnsibleSpecs/slices/backlog/012_kubecoder_argo_cutover/slice.md:113-118 (item 14, 'From B.3, held back deliberately to this point' — the R4 entry R2 joins)
